By 2013, EFF had spent seven years arguing in court that the National Security Agency was sweeping up ordinary Americans’ communications, including through the secret room that whistleblower Mark Klein had exposed. The government would neither confirm nor deny it, and outside the courtroom the public seemed to have moved on.   

Then, in early June, documentary filmmaker Laura Poitras and journalist Glenn Greenwald mysteriously missed a Freedom of the Press Foundation board meeting at EFF’s offices. It turned out they were in Hong Kong, meeting an NSA contractor who had been secretly writing to Laura for months. His name was Edward Snowden, he had thousands of secret documents proving the government had in fact been spying on millions of Americans. When he subsequently revealed himself, a photo of him sitting behind his laptop – emblazoned with a big red EFF sticker – went worldwide.  

Welcome to the fourth episode of “Privacy’s Defenders,” a podcast about the people – lawyers, journalists, hackers, and others – who’ve fought to secure your digital liberties since before most people even knew what the internet was.

In this episode, former EFF Executive Director Cindy Cohn talks with Laura Poitras about how she got to that historic moment, including her years of expertise in communicating via encrypted channels. Freedom of the Press Foundation Executive Director Trevor Timm – a former EFF activist – shares his recollection of the day the first Snowden story broke. For EFF and its clients in Jewel v. NSA, Snowden’s documents were proof of what the government had spent years refusing to confirm. As Cindy puts it, “We were struggling along in the mud, and we felt like somebody gave us wings.”  

It's the story of the lawyers who fought for your privacy, the government that lied about spying on you, and the whistleblower who blew it all wide open.  

The “Privacy’s Defenders” podcast is a follow-up to Cindy’s book, “Privacy’s Defender: My Thirty-Year Fight Against Digital Surveillance,” bringing to life pivotal moments in the voices of those who fought for your rights. Sales of “Privacy’s Defender” benefit EFF, so pick up your copy today!   

Joanne Elgart Jennings co-produced and created this podcast.    

Jarrod Sport co-produced, mixed, and mastered it.    

Corinne Ruff is our story editor.  

We had additional help from Rachel Estabrook and Alison Broverman.  

The original music was composed and performed by Nat Keefe of Hot Buttered Rum with Ben Andrews on the fiddle.
